A module that both imports and re-exports from the same specifier keeps both kinds in oxcruise (`import` and `export`); dependency-cruiser keeps only the first. oxcruise merges the kinds of duplicate dependencies instead of dropping information.

AMD module ids without a leading ./ are resolved by requirejs against `baseUrl`/`paths`. oxcruise has no requirejs config support and resolves them like package specifiers, so they are reported unresolved.

JSDoc imports (`@import`, `import("x")` in JSDoc comments) are always extracted by oxcruise. dependency-cruiser only detects them with `detectJSDocImports` AND `typescript` installed, and this run has no `typescript`. The module or edge exists in oxcruise only because of a JSDoc import; an import that is also written as a JSDoc import additionally gets the `jsdoc` and `type-only` kinds.

`exoticRequireStrings` is merged into `calls`. A callee in `calls` counts as an ES import (`import` condition) unless its name starts with `require`; dependency-cruiser treats exotic require strings as CommonJS requires.

`new URL("./x", import.meta.url)` and `new Worker(new URL(..))` are always dependencies in oxcruise (the `extract.skipUrls` switch is gone); dependency-cruiser has no such dependency. Modules and edges that are reachable only through one are listed under this kind too.
